candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — visitor respiratory screening
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that visitor respiratory-symptom screening helps identify potentially infectious persons and supports layered prevention of respiratory-pathogen introduction and transmission in healthcare settings.

options.A: To identify only bacterial infections because viral respiratory illnesses are not relevant to visitor infection-control measures.
options.B: To replace hand hygiene, source control, ventilation, and other infection-prevention measures in the facility.
options.C: To help identify potentially infectious visitors and reduce introduction or spread of respiratory pathogens as one component of layered infection prevention.
options.D: To permanently exclude all visitors because visitor precautions cannot be adjusted to symptoms, transmission conditions, or facility risk assessment.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC healthcare guidance uses layered measures to reduce respiratory-virus transmission. During periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity, facilities may use rapid screening/triage approaches, and visitors with respiratory symptoms should be advised about source control and encouraged to defer non-urgent routine visits until recovered. Screening is therefore one component of infection prevention, not a replacement for hand hygiene, source control, environmental controls, or other measures. C is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Healthcare facilities may use screening/triage and visitor symptom guidance during periods of increased community respiratory-virus activity as part of layered measures to reduce viral respiratory transmission.
candidate.source_document_title: Preventing Transmission of Viral Respiratory Pathogens in Healthcare Settings
